newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Spain, Russia forge new ties during king's visit.
newsitem.headline: Spain, Russia forge new ties during king's visit.

text.p: Spanish King Juan Carlos, rounding off a three-day visit to Moscow, invited Russian President Boris Yeltsin to Spain to maintain what the two sides said on Wednesday was a new momentum in bilateral relations.

The visit by Juan Carlos and his wife, Queen Sofia, to Moscow was largely ceremonial, giving Moscow an opportunity to show off religious and architectural treasures which have been resurrected since the fall of communism in 1991.
But they also brought dozens of Spanish business people to Russia to try to boost trade and investment between the two countries.

Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said work would be stepped up on documents covering defence of investments and preventing dual taxation so they could be signed when Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin visits Spain later this year.

Matutes had tried to soothe relations between Moscow and NATO, but his talks were overshadowed by intensive negotiations between Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana in Luxembourg.

On Wednesday the king, who last visited Moscow under communism in 1984, toured the construction site of the huge cathedral in Moscow which is being rebuilt on the site where the origninal was blown up by Soviet dicatator Josef Stalin.

He also toured a meat factory, a joint venture between Spain in Russia which Itar-Tass news agency said controlled 20 percent of the capital's meat market. The factory, Campomos, is one of 100 Russian-Spanish joint-ventures in Russia, Tass said.
The king and queen then opened an exhibition of Spanish art at the Pushkin museum, which includes paintings by Pablo Picasso, Joan Miro and Salvador Dali.

Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Igor Ivanov told a news briefing that Yeltsin, who last visited Madrid in 1994, had accepted Juan Carlos' invitation to pay another official visit to Spain at a date yet to be agreed.
Both Ivanov and Matutes told the briefing that the visit had given new momentum to bilateral relations.
